subject: URGENT: Helix Labs - production latency & 5xx spike (KV prefetch config)
messages:
From: Amina Rahman <support@helixlabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-leads@helixlabs.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency and 5xx spike — started ~08:45 PT

Jonas,

We started seeing a production-wide latency increase and 5xx errors on our inference routes at ~08:45 PT this morning. P99 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s and roughly 3% of requests returned 5xx over the first 30 minutes. Our engineers saw clear `KV cache miss -> long tail` correlation in our metrics; logs attached.

This is impacting our critical batch scoring jobs — we have a couple of enterprise jobs that must complete before EOD. Can Redwood confirm whether any config or rollout changed on your side, and what mitigation steps you can take immediately?

We appreciate quick updates — Helix is on standby to route traffic or accept suggested mitigations.

Thanks,
Amina Rahman
Support Lead, Helix Labs

Attachments (excerpt): svc_logs_excerpt.txt
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:28:17 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Production latency and 5xx spike — started ~08:45 PT

Team — Amina just opened an incident (JIRA-INC-9342). Quick summary: Helix sees p99 jump + 5xx correlated with KV cache miss patterns. They called out heavy batch scoring runs this morning.

Immediate asks:
- Laura / Marissa: can you confirm whether the recent prefetch window tweak we rolled last night (lowered to prefetch=3 -> changed eviction heuristics) could be causing head-of-line (HOL) blocking or cache thrash at scale? They reported sustained misses + eviction churn.
- Monica: can you run a fast-sim with their token distribution (I saved the small sample in Drive link below) and see if prefetch/eviction interacts badly with their long-tail sequences?
- Ben: I'll need a customer-facing status update in ~20–30m; keep it calibrated on mitigation & timeline.

I attached the KV config snapshot we have for their tenant. If this is a config regression, we should prepare an emergency rollback to previous prefetch/evict values and a temporary routing change (route heavy scoring to dedicated pool). Laura — recommend we prepare a short runbook with steps and confirmations.

Links: https://redwood.sharedrive/Helix/incident-9342-logs
JIRA-INC-9342

-Jonas

---- Forwarded message attached below ----
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:02:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency and 5xx spike — started ~08:45 PT

Jonas — quick technical summary from initial triage (ops/runtime):

What we see:
- Around 08:30 PT the tenant's priority lane saw an increase in unique prefix churn (many long-tail prefixes from batch scoring).
- Our metric `kv.evict.rate` rose by ~4x and `kv.prefetch.inflight` spiked, causing head-of-line stalls on several worker threads. Threads waiting on remote KV prefetches caused downstream request queuing -> p99 inflation and transient 5xx when request timeouts hit.
- The config we rolled last night reduced the prefetch aggressiveness but also increased per-prefix TTL to favor cache residency; this combination appears to amplify eviction/miss oscillations under their workload.

Immediate mitigation options (pros/cons):
1) Roll back prefetch config to previous baseline (prefetch.window=8, eviction.threshold=0.6) — fastest to test and revert. Lower risk to correctness. Expected customer-visible improvement within 5–10m of rollout.
2) Short-term routing: split heavy batch scoring to a dedicated pool (dedicated capacity) for Helix if their contract allows burst lanes — avoids touching global config but requires infra ops (ETA 20–40m).
3) Aggressive eviction tuning + per-tenant pinning: force smaller per-tenant max-resident set to prevent thrash. This mitigates oscillation but may increase miss rate for interactive traffic. Risky during business hours.

Recommended path: rollout option #1 immediately (rollback to last night's baseline) while preparing option #2 if rollback insufficient. I'll assemble the rollback commandset and verification checks now. I'll also capture `kv.get.latency` histograms pre/post and share.

Attachments: kv_config_snapshot.yaml (current), mitigation_playbook.pdf (draft runbook)

-Laura (runtime lead)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amina Rahman <support@helixlabs.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:25:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike — started ~08:45 PT

Amina — thanks for the quick report and the log excerpt. We're on it. Short customer note while the team investigates:

Hi Amina / Helix team —
We identified a runtime interaction with the KV prefetch/eviction config that can cause cache churn under high unique-prefix batch workloads. Our engineering team recommends a rollback to the previous prefetch/evict values immediately; we expect p99 to return to baseline within ~10 minutes of the change. We're preparing the rollback now and will confirm when complete.

We will also offer a one-time credits adjustment for today's impacted window while we finalize a longer-term per-tenant configuration to prevent recurrence. I will follow up with a formal summary and ticket (JIRA-INC-9342) by EOD.

If you want a dedicated lane for high-volume batch scoring, we can discuss options — it would take ~4–6 hours to provision and validate for Helix.

—Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amina Rahman <support@helixlabs.com>, ops-leads@helixlabs.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 18:30:00 -0800
Subject: Helix incident update & confirmed mitigation (rollback applied) — JIRA-INC-9342

Amina / Helix Ops —

Update and timeline (final):
- 2026-11-12 10:10 PT: team executed rollback to previous KV prefetch/eviction baseline (prefetch.window=8, eviction.threshold=0.6) for Helix tenant. Change deployed to priority lane only.
- 10:12 PT: observed `kv.evict.rate` return to normal ranges; p99 improved from ~1.8s to ~240ms within two rolling minutes. 5xx error rate dropped to baseline.
- 10:40 PT: to prevent recurrence we provisioned a temporary dedicated pool for Helix scoring jobs and routed batch workload there (validated). This extra capacity eliminated head-of-line impacts on interactive routes.

Attachments: mitigation_playbook.pdf (final) — contains rollback commands, verification checks, and recommended long-term config (per-tenant pinning + workload-aware prefetch profiles).

Next steps (recommendations for Helix + Redwood):
1) Accept dedicated pool for batch scoring (we propose a 4-hour provisioning window to harden and automate routing).
2) Work with our applied ML/serving team to produce a tailored prefetch profile based on your token-length distribution (Monica + Laura will lead).
3) Redwood to issue a one-time service credit for today’s impact; Ben will coordinate and send a formal credit note.

Thanks for patience and for the clear logs — that made root cause identification much faster. If you need a follow-up exec briefing, we can schedule a 30-minute sync with our CTO and your VP of Infrastructure.

-Jonas Weber
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
